coverage_notes:
This exhaustive survey swept four primary angles: (1) the foundational Shneiderman-Maes debate on direct manipulation vs. intelligent agents, including seminal works from both researchers and covering the CHI 97 debate papers; (2) modern instantiations of this debate in the context of LLM-based interfaces, prompt engineering vs. direct manipulation, and copilot vs. autonomous agents; (3) supporting HCI theory from seminal authors (Norman on affordances, Munzner on visualization, Pirolli on information foraging, Horvitz on mixed-initiative systems, Lieberman on learning agents); (4) contemporary research on trust calibration, transparency, explainability, cognitive load, agency, and reversibility in agent systems. 

Deduplication strategy: Removed duplicate URLs appearing across multiple search results (e.g., DirectGPT, mixed-initiative papers appeared 3-4 times). Prioritized open-access/arXiv versions where available. Organized 60+ unique sources into four tiers reflecting rigor and authority. Named authorities covered: Shneiderman, Maes, Norman, Tufte, Munzner, Pirolli, Lieberman, Horvitz, Völkel et al. (meta-analysis).

Notable gaps/deferrals: Limited inclusion of proprietary analyst reports (Gartner, Forrester) marked reference-only; some paywalled ACM/Springer papers listed with best-known URLs; trademark-specific copilot/agent vendor docs noted but deprioritized in favor of research-grounded sources. No significant theoretical angles left unswept—coverage includes both classical HCI theory (affordances, mental models, locus of control, agency) and cutting-edge LLM-agent interface challenges (trust in opaque systems, transparency mechanisms, autonomy calibration).

sources.title: Direct manipulation vs. interface agents
sources.notes: Seminal 1997 Interactions magazine debate between Shneiderman (championing direct manipulation and user control) and Maes (advocating intelligent agents for task automation). Foundational text defining the core tension. Cited 584+ times.

sources.title: Designing the User Interface: Strategies for Effective Human-Computer Interaction (4th Edition)
sources.notes: Shneiderman's canonical textbook articulating direct manipulation principles: continuous representation, physical actions, immediate feedback, reversibility. Multiple editions (1987-present) define the HCI field.

sources.title: Direct Manipulation Techniques for the Human-Computer Interface
sources.notes: Shneiderman's foundational 1981 paper introducing the term 'direct manipulation' and articulating the three core principles: continuous representation, physical actions (vs. syntax), rapid/incremental/reversible operations.

sources.title: Intelligent Software Agents vs. User-Controlled Direct Manipulation: A Debate
sources.notes: Maes' response articulating the case for intelligent agents to reduce cognitive burden in complex environments. Defends agent autonomy and learning from observation as complement to direct control.

sources.title: The Design of Everyday Things
sources.notes: Donald Norman's seminal 1988 work (originally 'Psychology of Everyday Things') introducing affordances to design community. Foundational for understanding how users perceive control and predictability in interfaces.

sources.title: Affordances and Design
sources.notes: Norman's direct essay on affordances (perceived possible actions) vs. reality. Critical for understanding how interfaces communicate control and agency to users, distinguishing real from perceived affordances.

sources.title: What is 'Intelligent' in Intelligent User Interfaces? A Meta-Analysis of 25 Years of IUI
sources.notes: Meta-analysis analyzing 25 years of IUI conference proceedings (Völkel et al., 2020). Text analysis extracting implicit definitions of 'intelligence'—reveals community conflates automation, adaptation, and interaction; no consensus definition.

sources.title: DirectGPT: A Direct Manipulation Interface to Interact with Large Language Models
sources.notes: Modern instantiation of Shneiderman's direct manipulation principles applied to LLM interaction. Argues direct manipulation (visual UI) reduces ambiguity and unpredictability vs. prompt engineering (natural language).

sources.title: Sensemaking in Multi-Agent LLM Interfaces: How Users Interpret Transparency and Trustworthiness Cues
sources.notes: CHI 2026 paper addressing how users interpret transparency cues in multi-agent LLM systems. Bridges classical HCI trust research with modern agent design challenges.

sources.title: People, Agents, and Interaction: Principles of Mixed-Initiative User Interfaces
sources.notes: Horvitz's foundational framework for mixed-initiative systems where humans and agents fluidly negotiate control. Introduces 'elegant coupling' concept and attention-sensitive interface design.

sources.title: Mixed-initiative interaction
sources.notes: Seminal work formalizing mixed-initiative principles. Addresses when agent should take initiative vs. relinquish control, seamless handoffs, and transparent negotiation of agency.

sources.title: Principles of mixed-initiative user interfaces
sources.notes: CHI conference paper establishing design principles for mixed-initiative UIs. Addresses turn-taking, visibility of agent intent, and human override capability.

sources.title: Mixed-Initiative Control: AI Design Patterns
sources.notes: Contemporary design pattern library for mixed-initiative systems. Emphasizes ownership clarity, human priority, explicit handoffs, and conflict resolution—practical application of Horvitz principles.

sources.title: Agents for the User Interface
sources.notes: Lieberman & Selker's foundational MIT Media Lab work on interface agents. Proposes teacher-student relationship metaphor; introduces programming-by-example for teaching agents without explicit code.

sources.title: Autonomous Interface Agents
sources.notes: Lieberman's CHI paper on autonomous agents that learn from user behavior via observation. Addresses challenge of creating agents that don't require explicit programming while maintaining user control.

sources.title: A learning interface agent for scheduling meetings
sources.notes: Early IUI '94 paper demonstrating learning agents in practice. Agent learns user preferences through observation (master-apprentice model) for calendar scheduling—precursor to modern learning agents.

sources.title: Information Foraging Theory: Adaptive Interaction with Information
sources.notes: Pirolli's foundational theory applying ecological foraging concepts to information-seeking. Core concept of 'information scent' explains how users navigate complex systems—relevant to agent interface design and discoverability.

sources.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information
sources.notes: Tufte's seminal work on information design. 'Clutter and confusion are failures of design, not attributes of information'—principle underlying visibility and control in agent interfaces.

sources.title: Visual Design of the User Interface (ET Booklet)
sources.notes: Tufte's 16-page 1989 booklet for IBM on interface design principles. Emphasizes design information before polish; user-centered approach to visibility—foundational for agent UI transparency.

sources.title: Visualization Analysis and Design
sources.notes: Munzner's comprehensive textbook on visualization design. Nested model (domain → abstraction → encoding → algorithm) applicable to agent interface design, emphasizing task-data alignment.

sources.title: Interface agents: A review of the field
sources.notes: Comprehensive survey of interface agent literature. Defines agent types, discusses Maes' framework, and identifies design challenges around transparency and user control.

sources.title: Direct Manipulation vs. Interface Agents: Revisiting the Classic HCI Debate Decades Later
sources.notes: Contemporary practitioner synthesis (Sonia MH Wu, 2025) revisiting Shneiderman-Maes debate. Advocates hybrid approach: transparency, human oversight, progressive automation. Key insight: 'exceptional agent without thoughtful UI is destined for POC graveyard.'

sources.title: Direct Manipulation: Definition
sources.notes: Nielsen Norman Group essay (Sherugar & Budiu, 2024) on direct manipulation principles. Balances benefits (visibility, feedback, learning) vs. limitations (bulk operations, accessibility). Foundational reference.

sources.title: The agentic interface: principles and patterns for autonomous User Experiences
sources.notes: Medium essay on agentic UI principles. Emphasizes balance between autonomy and control, visibility of agent reasoning, and progressive disclosure—practical application of HCI theory to modern agents.

sources.title: Toward a Human-Centered Evaluation Framework for Trustworthy LLM-Powered GUI Agents
sources.notes: arXiv paper proposing evaluation framework for LLM-based agents. Addresses predictability, transparency, and user control challenges specific to LLM agents vs. classical agents.

sources.title: Enhancing Trust in LLM-Based AI Automation Agents: New Considerations and Future Challenges
sources.notes: arXiv survey on trust in LLM agents. Argues transparency of goals/capabilities/reasoning more critical than reliability itself; identifies design patterns for trust-building in opaque systems.

sources.title: AI Chains: Transparent and Controllable Human-AI Interaction by Chaining Large Language Model Prompts
sources.notes: ResearchGate paper proposing prompt chaining for transparent agent behavior. Addresses unpredictability of monolithic LLM prompts vs. visible multi-step decomposition.

sources.title: AI Transparency in the Age of LLMs: A Human-Centered Research Roadmap
sources.notes: arXiv roadmap on LLM transparency challenges. Argues fluency masks inaccuracy; proposes human-centered research agenda for transparency mechanisms in LLM-based systems.

sources.title: Understanding the LLM-ification of CHI: Unpacking the Impact of LLMs at CHI through a Systematic Literature Review
sources.notes: CHI 2025 systematic review examining LLM papers at CHI. Reveals paradigm shift from traditional AI transparency norms; reviewers demand technical details to validate LLM claims.

sources.title: Reporting and Reviewing LLM-Integrated Systems in HCI: Challenges and Considerations
sources.notes: CHI 2026 paper on methodological challenges in evaluating LLM-integrated interfaces. Addresses how to assess transparency, failure modes, and boundary conditions in agent systems.

sources.title: Explainability in Human-Agent Systems
sources.notes: arXiv paper defining explainability and its relationship to transparency, interpretability, and faithfulness in agent systems. Foundational for understanding why explanations matter to users.

sources.title: Explainable Interface for Human-Autonomy Teaming: A Survey
sources.notes: Survey of explainability interfaces in human-agent teaming. Comprehensive review of design patterns, evaluation methods, and user studies on how explanations affect trust and performance.

sources.title: Human-XAI Interaction: A Review and Design Principles for Explanation User Interfaces
sources.notes: Springer chapter on designing interfaces for AI explanations. Focuses on how to present agent reasoning/decisions to users in ways that build trust without overwhelming.

sources.title: Because we have LLMs, we Can and Should Pursue Agentic Interpretability
sources.notes: arXiv position paper arguing LLMs enable better interpretability than classical agents. Proposes agentic interpretability (understanding agent reasoning) as critical for trust vs. model interpretability.

sources.title: Adaptive trust calibration for human-AI collaboration
sources.notes: PLOS One study on trust calibration in human-AI teams. Shows transparency alone insufficient for recovering from over-trust; proposes adaptive calibration interventions.

sources.title: Calibrating Reliance on Automated Advice: Transparency and Trust Calibration Feedback
sources.notes: Theoretical framework and user study on transparency's role in trust calibration. Identifies feedback mechanisms that help users develop accurate mental models of agent capabilities.

sources.title: Measuring and Understanding Trust Calibrations for Automated Systems: A Survey of the State-Of-The-Art and Future Directions
sources.notes: CHI survey on trust calibration measurement methods. Comprehensive review of how to assess whether users develop appropriate trust in agents; identifies design implications.

sources.title: Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability
sources.notes: arXiv position paper proposing scientific foundations for assessing agent reliability. Argues current evaluation methods insufficient for building user trust in autonomous systems.

sources.title: The key role of design and transparency in enhancing trust in AI-powered digital agents
sources.notes: ScienceDirect paper emphasizing design's role in transparency. Argues UI design choices (what information to show, when, how) shape user trust independent of underlying agent capability.

sources.title: Autonomy Reshapes How Personalization Affects Privacy Concerns and Trust in LLM Agents
sources.notes: arXiv study showing autonomy level affects how users perceive privacy and trust tradeoffs. Counterintuitive finding: higher autonomy agents sometimes increase perceived control if designed well.

sources.title: Why Johnny Can't Use Agents: Industry Aspirations vs. User Realities with AI Agent Software
sources.notes: arXiv paper documenting user failures with autonomous agents. Identifies disconnect between agent capabilities and user expectations; proposes design principles for transparency and control.

sources.title: Engaging with AI: How Interface Design Shapes Human-AI Collaboration in High-Stakes Decision-Making
sources.notes: arXiv paper on interface design in high-stakes scenarios (medicine, finance). Shows transparency and control mechanisms critical when agent errors have serious consequences.

sources.title: Dark Patterns Meet GUI Agents: LLM Agent Susceptibility to Manipulative Interfaces and the Role of Human Oversight
sources.notes: arXiv paper on adversarial agent interfaces. Shows agents vulnerable to UI manipulation; identifies human oversight patterns that mitigate risks—extends control concerns to agent-agent interaction.

sources.title: Engineering Trust, Creating Vulnerability: A Socio-Technical Analysis of AI Interface Design
sources.notes: arXiv critical analysis of trust in AI interface design. Argues transparency mechanisms can paradoxically increase vulnerability by creating false confidence; proposes accountability frameworks.

sources.title: Understanding Agency in Human-Computer Interaction Design
sources.notes: ResearchGate paper on agency concept in HCI. Defines user agency as perceived ability to influence/control systems; critical for balancing autonomy with human oversight.

sources.title: The experience of agency in human-computer interactions: a review
sources.notes: Frontiers review of sense of agency in HCI. Neuroscientific perspective on how users experience control; shows direct manipulation fosters stronger agency than automation.

sources.title: The role of user's perceived control in interface design, employing verbal protocol analysis
sources.notes: Classic ergonomics paper on perceived control in interface design. Uses protocol analysis to show users value sense of control over actual efficiency—foundational for agent UI design.

sources.title: Levels of Autonomy for AI Agents
sources.notes: arXiv paper proposing autonomy taxonomy for agents. Ranges from user-controlled (copilot model) to fully autonomous; discusses design implications at each level.

sources.title: Distinguishing Autonomous AI Agents from Collaborative Agentic Systems: A Comprehensive Framework
sources.notes: arXiv framework distinguishing autonomy levels. Identifies tradeoff between agent independence and user control; proposes design patterns for different autonomy models.

sources.title: ResearStudio: A Human-Intervenable Framework for Building Controllable Deep-Research Agents
sources.notes: arXiv system paper on human-in-the-loop research agents. Demonstrates practical patterns for human intervention at multiple decision points—instantiates mixed-initiative principles.

sources.title: Terminal Is All You Need: Design Properties for Human-AI Agent Collaboration
sources.notes: arXiv paper on CLI as interface for agent collaboration. Shows explicit turn-taking (user at prompt by default) enables human oversight; contrasts with opaque background automation.

sources.title: AgentBuilder: Exploring Scaffolds for Prototyping User Experiences of Interface Agents
sources.notes: arXiv design tool paper. Scaffolds for rapidly prototyping agent interfaces; identified design patterns from user testing (transparency, control, status) critical for adoption.

sources.title: From Conversation to Orchestration: HCI Challenges and Opportunities in Interactive Multi-Agentic Systems
sources.notes: HAI 2024 paper on multi-agent interface challenges. Proposes making internal agent dialogues visible (graphs, timelines) to support user understanding and oversight.

sources.title: Delegate the Undoable, Guard the Irreversible: Tiering Agent Autonomy by Reversibility
sources.notes: Practitioner essay proposing reversibility-based autonomy scaling. Two-way door operations (editable) warrant higher autonomy; one-way doors (permanent) need approval—operationalizes Shneiderman's reversibility principle.

sources.title: Expose System State: A Primer of Human-Agent Interaction Guidelines
sources.notes: Contemporary design guidelines (June 2026) on system visibility. Emphasizes ambient intelligibility vs. constant interruption; proposes state exposure patterns for agent interfaces.

sources.title: Visibility of System Status (Usability Heuristic #1)
sources.notes: Nielsen Norman Group essay on first usability heuristic. Applies visibility principle to agent systems: real-time state exposure critical for user mental models and trust.

sources.title: To design interfaces for exploratory data analysis, we need theories of graphical inference
sources.notes: arXiv paper on exploratory UI design. Argues for visibility and reversibility in data exploration—principles equally applicable to exploratory agent interactions.

sources.title: Human-Computer Collaboration for Visual Analytics: an Agent-based Framework
sources.notes: arXiv framework for collaborative agent-user visual analytics. Demonstrates how agent recommendations (vs. autonomous actions) preserve user control while providing assistance.

sources.title: Discovering the Sweet Spot of Human-Computer Configurations: A Case Study in Information Extraction
sources.notes: arXiv case study on agent-human collaboration. Identifies optimal point between full automation and manual control; shows mixed-initiative outperforms both extremes.

sources.title: Designing for Autonomy: UX Principles for Agentic AI
sources.notes: UXmatters essay (2025) on autonomy design principles. Emphasizes: don't jump to full autonomy, visibility prevents anxiety, design autonomy progressively as trust earned.

sources.title: Agentic AI Design Patterns(2026 Edition)
sources.notes: Medium essay on 2026 agentic patterns: Reflection, Tool Use, Planning, Multi-Agent Collaboration, Orchestrator-Worker, Evaluator-Optimizer. Emphasizes sandbox mode for safe exploration.

sources.title: What Are the Must-Know Agentic Design Patterns for 2026?
sources.notes: Medium essay on essential agentic patterns. Highlights conversational UI beyond chat, multi-agent dashboards, trust-building transparency, adaptive personalization.

sources.title: Agentic Design Patterns: The 2026 Guide to Building Autonomous Systems
sources.notes: SitePoint guide to agentic patterns. Emphasizes shift from UI-centric to AI-driven collaboration; user expects variable control levels and progressive autonomy.

sources.title: Agent UX: designing UI for AI agents in 2026
sources.notes: FuseLab creative agency essay on agent UX. Four principles: transparency, user control, proactive status, structured error recovery—any interface missing one sees post-month churn.

sources.title: Agentic Workflows for Conversational Human-AI Interaction Design
sources.notes: arXiv design framework for conversational agent workflows. Proposes interaction patterns balancing exploratory (open inquiry) and confirmatory (accept/reject) agent behaviors.

sources.title: Effect of anthropomorphism and perceived intelligence in chatbot avatars of visual design on user experience
sources.notes: Frontiers paper on anthropomorphism in agent design. Shows human-like features increase engagement but can inflate trust beyond actual capability—design tradeoff identified.

sources.title: How Users Perceive Mixed-Initiative AI: Attitudes Toward Assistance in Problem Solving
sources.notes: arXiv user study on mixed-initiative perceptions. Identifies when users prefer agent suggestions vs. full autonomy; proposes design patterns for communicating agent capabilities.

sources.title: Toward Safe and Responsible AI Agents: A Three-Pillar Model for Transparency, Accountability, and Trustworthiness
sources.notes: arXiv framework for responsible agent design. Three pillars: transparency (how agent decides), accountability (tracing decisions), trustworthiness (reliability + user confidence).

sources.title: DuoZone: A User-Centric, LLM-Guided Mixed-Initiative XR Window Management System
sources.notes: arXiv system paper on mixed-initiative window management. Demonstrates zone-based ownership (user/agent/shared) as practical pattern for avoiding control conflicts.

sources.title: MAESTRO: Adapting GUIs and Guiding Navigation with User Preferences in Conversational Agents with GUIs
sources.notes: arXiv system for user-preference-aware GUI agents. Shows how to surface and respect user preferences in autonomous navigation—preserves control through declarative constraints.

sources.title: From Human Interfaces to Agent Interfaces: Rethinking Software Design in the Age of AI-Native Systems
sources.notes: arXiv position paper on paradigm shift from human-first to agent-first interface design. Proposes design patterns that support both human interaction and agent orchestration.

sources.title: Theory-based approach for assessing cognitive load during time-critical resource-managing human–computer interactions
sources.notes: Springer paper on cognitive load in HCI. Shows agent interfaces increase cognitive load when transparency is poor; visibility reduces overload.

sources.title: AI Agent Behavioral Science
sources.notes: arXiv survey on behavioral science applied to agent design. Addresses psychological factors affecting trust, control perception, and user adoption of autonomous systems.

sources.title: Data Agent: A Holistic Architecture for Orchestrating Data+AI Ecosystems
sources.notes: arXiv architecture paper on data agents. Proposes serving dual audiences (human & agent); addresses how interface design must support both goal-setting and autonomous execution.
